details:
- CVE-2026-53783: fix a TOCTOU escape from rrsync's restricted directory by
  replacing the lexical-only Perl support/rrsync with upstream's Python one,
  which pins each validated path component through /proc/self/fd, fails closed
  on path anomalies, pins the receiver option directories a peer can pivot
  (--backup-dir, --partial-dir, alt-dest) and denies --copy-unsafe-links,
  device/special creation, a peer-selected --debug, remote --files-from in
  write-only mode and the no-overwrite auxiliary paths inside a restricted dir
- NOTE: the replacement needs the new --drop-D option, backported from upstream
  b607369f; it makes a receiver refuse to create devices and special files
  without changing the file-list encoding the way --no-D does. support/ keeps
  shipping as non-executable documentation, so no installed program changes
  behaviour unless an operator has wired rrsync as an SSH forced command.
  rrsync is now Python rather than Perl
- NOTE: one receiver-side spelling differs from upstream deliberately: a
  destination that already exists and is not a directory is pinned by its
  parent rather than by itself, because rsync replaces such a destination by
  unlinking its name, which the self-pin spelling cannot support -- without
  this, pushing a file onto an existing file through rrsync failed. Path
  components above the destination stay pinned either way
